messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: High 429 rate detected — inference-cluster-eu1 — 5m spike, 12% error-rate vs 0.3% baseline. Paging oncall.
jamie (oncall-sre): ack. seeing 429s across /v1/generate and /v1/embeddings. dashboard: https://dash.redwood.internal/boards/429-eu1 :warning:
sasha (eng-platform): I can pull pods/allocations. any tenant pattern? metrics show embeddings throughput jump +10x for a subset of tenants.
mike (infra): infra-side: GPU hosts healthy, but queue depth is rising on grpc-proxy nodes. suspect ingress throttles or KV cache misses.
jamie (oncall-sre): noted. starting mitigation plan: 1) short-term global QPS cut for non-critical routes 2) enable per-tenant shaping for top offenders 3) disable non-essential background collectors. starting step 1 now.
ara (prodops): good. please post exact commands so PMs/CS know what we did.
jamie (oncall-sre): running RateCare adjust: ```
# reduce global burst and baseline QPS for public tier
ratecare-cli set-policy --scope=global --route=/v1/embeddings --qps=8 --burst=16 --reason="emergency 429 mitigation"
``` 
jamie (oncall-sre): applied. watch for downstream 429 delta.
leo (customer-success): heads up — CS is seeing two customers reporting degraded latency. I'll draft comms once we understand scope.
sasha (eng-platform): quick tenant breakdown: top 3 tenants responsible for 72% of the extra token volume. starting surgical per-tenant shaping for those 3.
jamie (oncall-sre): per-tenant shaping commands: ```
# per-tenant QPS cap
ratecare-cli set-policy --tenant=tenant-42 --route=/v1/embeddings --qps=2 --burst=4
ratecare-cli set-policy --tenant=tenant-83 --route=/v1/generate --qps=1
``` 
mike (infra): applied on RateCare edge. also toggled embed-cache read-path to prefer local cache (falls back to global). hoping this lowers KV miss thrash.
jamie (oncall-sre): immediate telemetry: 429 rate dropped from 12% -> 6% in 60s. queue depth stable-ish. latency still elevated for some p95s.
ara (prodops): can we disable low-priority features (syntax-highlighting service, usage-collector) to free tokens? those are safe to cut for a window.
sasha (eng-platform): deploying quick feature-flag cut: ```
ffctl disable --service=usage-collector --env=prod
ffctl disable --service=syntax-highlighting --env=prod
``` 
sasha (eng-platform): flags are live.
jamie (oncall-sre): after flags: 429 down to 3.2% in 3m. embedding throughput for top tenants reduced as expected. still monitoring.
leo (customer-success): PS update: notified customers A and B — they appreciate the transparency. asked if we can provide ETA to full recovery.
jamie (oncall-sre): ETA tentative: if p95 latency and 429s settle under 1% in next 15–30 mins, we'll go to staged rollback of feature flags and restore less aggressive QPS caps.
mike (infra): adding guardrail: auto-fallback policy if 429 creeps >2% after rollback — will reapply tenant caps automatically for 10m.
ara (prodops): request: create a short incident note (one-liner + mitigation steps) so support can use it in responses.
jamie (oncall-sre): drafting: "429 spike due to sudden high embedding traffic + cache thrash; mitigations: global QPS reduction, per-tenant shaping, disabled non-essential collectors; ongoing telemetry." will paste to thread.
jamie (oncall-sre): pasted incident note into #incidents-log. link: https://wiki.redwood.internal/incidents/2026-03-15-429-eu1
sasha (eng-platform): observed root signals: a recent client-side SDK change increased concurrent prefix requests — I'll open a ticket with client-team and recommend backoff.
jamie (oncall-sre): OK team, likely a combination: client behavior + slightly degraded prefix cache hit-rate -> request amplification. our mitigations look to be effective.
ara (prodops): handoff plan: jamie stepping off at 2135550200 — @sasha you'll be next oncall. jamie please summarize runbook + current flags.
jamie (oncall-sre): summary for handoff: current state: 429 = 2.8%, p95 latency elevated but trending down. mitigations in place: global QPS policy (embeddings 8qps), tenant caps for tenant-42/83/99, usage-collector + syntax-highlighting flags disabled, edge cache preference toggled. rollback criteria: sustained 429 <1% and p95 stable for 3 consecutive 5m windows. rollback steps: re-enable flags, incrementally raise global qps by 25% every 5m, remove per-tenant caps if no regression. escalation: page infra lead (mike) if 429 >3% after rollback attempt.
sasha (eng-platform): got it. I'll monitor next 30m and own rollback. leaving a watch runbook note in the incident ticket.
leo (customer-success): I'll continue CS comms and share ETA when rollback begins.
jamie (oncall-sre): handing to @sasha. oncall-rotation: jamie out, sasha in.
sasha (eng-platform): acknowledged. I'm on it. creating a short checklist in thread and will update metrics every 5m. :clipboard:
mike (infra): standing by; if we see kernel OOMs or node pressure I'll post here and initiate host-level mitigation.
ara (prodops): thanks everyone. final note: please add any postmortem artifacts (dashboard slices, query ids) to the incident ticket for later RCA.
incident-bot: NOTE: this thread was auto-archived by incident-bot at 2135550345 after status set to "watching" by sasha."
